summary: Self-hostable AI second brain that answers from the web and your documents, with custom agents and scheduled research.

heroCommands.command: Open the cloud app at app.khoj.dev, or self-host it by following docs.khoj.dev

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Khoj is a personal AI app that scales from an on-device assistant to enterprise AI. It chats with local or online LLMs, answers from the internet and your documents, lets you create custom agents, and can automate research with newsletters and notifications.
sixtySeconds.problem: Your notes and files are scattered and general chatbots can't see them. Khoj searches and answers from your own documents as well as the web.
whoFor: People with large personal notes (Obsidian, Emacs, Notion)
Teams wanting a self-hosted AI assistant
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for an open-source, self-hostable assistant you can reach from the browser, Obsidian, Emacs, desktop, phone or WhatsApp.
requirements: A browser for the cloud app, or a machine to self-host

overview: Khoj chats with local or online models (Llama, Qwen, Gemma, Mistral, GPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek) and answers from the internet and your docs, including images, PDFs, Markdown, org-mode, Word and Notion files.
You can create agents with custom knowledge, persona, model and tools, schedule automated research, use semantic search, generate images and talk out loud.
Use the cloud app at app.khoj.dev or self-host it; the README points to the setup docs for self-hosting. An enterprise option exists. Khoj is AGPL-3.0 licensed.
